title: Reliability Cadre Onboarding + Rapid SLO Deployment Guide (2026)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working guide for forming a temporary Reliability Cadre — a small cross-functional team that runs a fast, standardized SLO definition-to-enforcement pipeline for 3 pilot services in Q2 2026. Goal is to prove a repeatable process that reduces time-to-first-SLO from ~6 weeks to ~2–3 sprints (4–6 weeks) with clear handoffs to service owners and ops.

Audience:
- SREs and service owners (engineering leads)
- Observability and platform teams
- Product / PMs for critical services

Scope / Constraints:
- Pilot scope: 3 customer-facing services chosen for diversity (low-latency API, long-polling batch job, and async ingestion).
- Cadre duration: 8 weeks (onboarding + two sprints + stabilization handoff).
- We will not rework infra across pilots; prefer safe config-level changes (alerts, SLIs, remediation playbooks).

Primary objectives (measurable):
1) Ship production-grade SLIs + SLOs + alerting for 3 pilots within 6 weeks.
2) Create a templated SLO definition artifact that service teams can adopt in <1 hour.
3) Validate alerting-to-escalation path and confirm one automated rollback or fallback for each pilot.
4) Produce post-mortem-lite template and teach 6 engineers how to run it.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Reliability Cadre Lead: Aisha Patel — overall coordination, unblock, escalation.
- Observability Lead: Marco Diaz — metrics, dashboards, tracing, log sampling.
- Platform/Infra SME: Lina Chen — deployment knobs, feature flags, safe rollout.
- Service Owner Liaisons: Assign one engineer per pilot (Samir Rao, Priya Menon, TBD).
- Exec Sponsor: VP SRE (name TBD) — priority and resourcing.

High-level timeline (8-week plan):
- Week 0 (Prep): finalize pilots, reserve cadence slots, create base dashboard template.
- Week 1 (Onboard sprint): SLI discovery, measurement proof-of-concept on staging, baseline metric capture.
- Week 2 (SLO draft): Define SLO targets with product and service owners; finalize alert thresholds.
- Week 3 (Deploy & validate): Push alerting + dashboard to prod (low-risk), enable synthetic checks.
- Week 4 (SLO enforcement): Tune alerts, run tabletop fail scenarios, add auto-remediation where safe.
- Week 5 (Stabilize): Burn-rate monitoring, adjust TTLs and paging policies.
- Week 6 (Handoff sprint): Deliver SLO artifact, runbook, and training session; transition to service ops.
- Week 7–8 (Follow-up): Monitor adoption, triage issues, gather feedback for core SLO template.

Sprint-by-sprint deliverables (concrete):
- Onboard sprint deliverables: SLI inventory doc per pilot; working Grafana/Tempo dashboard; synthetic probe plan.
- SLO draft deliverables: SLO YAML (templated), PR to service repo, acceptance criteria checklist.
- Deploy sprint deliverables: Alert rules in monitoring (prometheus / alertmanager), on-call rota updates, ops checklist.
- Handoff deliverables: Recorded training + 1-pager, post-handoff adoption metric snapshot.

Minimum Viable SLO template (example fields):
- service: <service-name>
- owner: <eng-lead-email>
- user-facing-boolean: true/false
- slis: [p99-latency-ms, request-success-rate, queue-depth]
- slo: {availability: 99.9%, latency-p99: 200ms} (expressed as time-window + target)
- measurement-window: 30d
- alerting: {severity: sev2 if burn-rate>1.0 for 1h, sev1 if sustained >2h} 
- remediation-playbook-link: <confluence url>

Onboarding checklist (quick):
- [ ] Kickoff with service owner (30m) — align on user journeys and business impact
- [ ] Inventory existing dashboards and SLIs (10–20m review)
- [ ] Attach synthetic checks for critical paths (HTTP / health / auth)
- [ ] Create SLO artifact PR and runbook stub
- [ ] Schedule tabletop for failover/test alerts

Telemetry + measurement notes (operational):
- Prefer direct counters over derived histograms where possible; histograms required for latency percentiles.
- Sampling: keep traces for 1% of requests by default for high-throughput services.
- Storage: 90-day retention for SLO signals (30d measurement window + 60d lookback for incidents).
- Alerting: use burn-rate math and absolute thresholds; avoid alert storms by grouping related symptoms.

Communication plan (internal):
- Weekly sync with Cadre + service owners (30m).
- Daily stand for first deploy week (15m).
- Slack channel per pilot (sre-pilot-<service>) — use +greencheck for deploys.
- Exec digest: 1-page status update every 2 weeks to VP SRE.

Launch day runbook (condensed):
1) Confirm baseline metrics pre-deploy (timestamped screenshot).
2) Apply SLO artifacts behind feature flag (if available).
3) Enable synthetic checks and verify green.
4) Turn on alerts to on-call (notify cadence).
5) Watch burn-rate and p99 for 2 hours; if sustained >1.5x expected, trigger rollback plan.

Rollback / fallback criteria (explicit):
- Any prod latency p99 > 2x SLO target for 30m AND error-rate > 0.5% absolute increase -> rollback.
- If auto-remediation runs 3x in 1 hour, stop remediation and page oncall.

Handoff & knowledge transfer:
- Deliverables: SLO YAML, Grafana dashboard link, Alertmanager rules, runbook (playbook), recording of training.
- Acceptance checklist for service owners: walk-through + signoff (Slack/PR comment).
- Post-handoff review at +2 weeks: adoption snapshot and feedback survey.

Success metrics for pilot program (to evaluate run):
- Time to first SLO (goal: <= 30 days from kickoff).
- Fraction of alerts with clear remediation steps (>90%).
- False-positive rate on new alerts (target <15% after tuning).
- Number of services adopting template within next 3 months (target 6).

Known dependencies & risks:
- Platform rate limits for metrics ingestion (may require batching or lower retention).
- Service owners capacity — need 1–2 engineers allocated per pilot sprint.
- Third-party monitoring plugin compatibility for synthetic probes.

Open questions (needs answers before Week 1):
- Who is the Exec Sponsor (we need prioritization)? -> action: Aisha to confirm by 2026-02-15.
- Can services accept a feature flag flow for alerting enablement? If not, must plan a low-risk roll.
- Any legal/compliance constraints for tracing retention on pilot services?

Action items (next 7 days):
- [Aisha] Finalize pilot list and post to slack channel (due 2026-02-14).
- [Marco] Create dashboard template and share example by 2026-02-16.
- [Lina] Validate alertmanager quotas and propose safeties by 2026-02-18.
- [Service owners] Nominate liaison engineers and confirm availability for sprint slots.

Notes / working thoughts (informal):
- Keep the first pilots conservative: prefer detection + human-in-the-loop remediation.
- Long-term: we want a self-serve SLO SDK that outputs SLO YAML + dashboards from a single command. That’s 2–3 quarters out.
- Consider combining this with ongoing reliability guild workshops for knowledge propagation.

Appendix: Example quick SLO YAML (MVP)
service: user-api
owner: user-api-lead@redwood.ai
measurement_window: 30d
slis:
  - name: request_success_rate
    type: ratio
    numerator: requests.status < 500
    denominator: requests.total
  - name: latency_p99_ms
    type: percentile
    histogram: request_latency_ms
slo:
  availability: 99.95%
  latency_p99: 200ms
alerting:
  - name: request_success_rate_burn
    condition: burn_rate(request_success_rate, 1h) > 1.0
    severity: sev2
    runbook: https://confluence.company/reliability/runbooks/user-api-success-rate

-- end of draft --

(Keep this doc as a living artifact — copy into each pilot folder and evolve per service.)
